messages:
Hannah (sales): NimbusTech POC blocked — their staging app can't complete TLS to our private endpoint from one set of subnets. Reports show cert mismatch and NXDOMAIN from different hosts. Can we triage? :rotating_light:

Nimbus-Network: From app-subnet-2 we get NXDOMAIN for private.redwood-nimbus.internal, from app-subnet-1 we get cert 'corp-inspect.local'. Management subnet resolves fine. Logs below.

Nimbus-Network: ```dig @10.10.0.2 private.redwood-nimbus.internal +short
;; -> no output (NXDOMAIN)

curl -v https://private.redwood-nimbus.internal/health
* Connected to 10.20.30.40 port 443
* TLS alert, unknown CA
* SSL: certificate subject name 'corp-inspect.local' does not match target host name 'private.redwood-nimbus.internal'```

Pri (neteng): Two separate symptoms: DNS (hosted zone not associated with the app VPC or resolver rule missing) + TLS inspection on the egress path for the other subnets. Which subnets map to which egress?

Nimbus-Network: app-subnet-1 -> transit-gw -> corp-egress-appliance (MITM). app-subnet-2 -> internal resolver 10.10.0.2 which returns NXDOMAIN. Management subnets use a different resolver and succeed. We also captured openssl from failing TLS host:

Nimbus-Network: ```openssl s_client -connect 10.20.30.40:443 -servername private.redwood-nimbus.internal -status
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = corp-inspect.local
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
OCSP response: no response sent
---
no peer certificate available
---
```

Ethan (solutions): That indicates the inspection proxy is replacing the cert and likely dropping OCSP stapling or blocking OCSP egress. For DNS, confirm whether the private hosted zone "private.redwood-nimbus.internal" is associated with the app VPC or not.

Nimbus-Network: Hosted zone is only associated with vpc-mgmt-01. App VPC vpc-app-02 is not associated. They assumed shared resolver rules would suffice.

Marco (eng-platform): Quick POC unblock options (ordered by invasiveness):
1) Provide a single dedicated POC IP (203.0.116.88) and ALB that terminates TLS with correct SANs; customer adds a one-line bypass for that IP so traffic avoids MITM and resolves to our IP — no zone changes needed.
2) Ask Nimbus to associate the private hosted zone with vpc-app-02 or create a Route53 inbound resolver endpoint (longer security review).
3) Provide a fallback server build that disables OCSP stapling and uses a slimmer cert chain so the inspection proxy is less likely to fail (temporary, less ideal).

Pri (neteng): Nimbus security is very strict about egress. They prefer 1) a single /32 bypass and short window over associating hosted zones. If you give them the IP and the exact window they'll raise a change ticket.

Ethan (solutions): We can detect the OCSP problem too — if their proxy blocks outbound to OCSP responders, doesnt forward stapled responses. For the record, OCSP responders are dynamic; we can provide a shortlist for demo hours (e.g., ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org IPs) but customers often won't open general egress.

Nimbus-Network: We'll allow two IPs for OCSP for 24 hours if you confirm them. But prefer route/bypass for single IP.

Marco (eng-platform): I'll stand up the ALB now with IP 203.0.116.88 and cert that includes private.redwood-nimbus.internal. We'll mark it POC-only and schedule teardown after 48 hours. deploy-bot: queued create-poc-alb(203.0.116.88) -> status: queued.

Ethan (solutions): I'll draft a short security note for Nimbus: what the bypass does, why it's temporary, rollback plan, and cert revocation timeline. Also list the OCSP IPs as a fallback.

Nimbus-Network: Change control: we'll apply a bypass for 203.0.116.88/32 for 48 hours once you confirm cert SANs and window. Please provide contact for rollback.

Marco (eng-platform): Cert SANs: private.redwood-nimbus.internal. Window: 48 hours starting when you apply the bypass. Contact: marco@redwood.com. Once ALB is live, post here and we can test.

deploy-bot: Allocation successful -> ALB(203.0.116.88) provisioning started.

Nimbus-Network: Bypass applied. Testing from previously failing hosts...

Nimbus-Network: ```curl -v https://private.redwood-nimbus.internal/health
* Connected to 203.0.116.88 (203.0.116.88) port 443
* TLS handshake complete
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{ "status": "ok" }```

Ethan (solutions): Awesome — demo unblocked. Please confirm you'll remove bypass after 48 hours and we'll decommission the ALB and revoke cert. We'll add a ticket to follow up with the permanent fix: hosted zone association or resolver endpoint.

Nimbus-Network: Confirmed. We'll revert bypass after 48 hours and will start security review for the long-term resolver association. Thanks everyone for the quick triage. :white_check_mark:
